a1.title: Having the audio graph connected costs a small, measurable amount of frame time on the street (about +1.4 ms p50, +2 to 4 ms p95, about twice as many frames over 34 ms)
a1.detail: My A/B ran on the same page with the graph pulled and not pulled: the old silent behaviour against the fixed audible one. Rounds 1 to 3, on vs off. p50: 18.1/16.7/16.7 vs 16.7/16.7/16.7. p95: 23.2/20.8/18.1 vs 19.3/16.7/16.7. Frames over 34 ms: 4, 8, 4 vs 2, 3, 2. The direction is the same in all three pairs. The machine is shared and round 0 was noise, so treat the size as about 1 to 2 ms with large uncertainty. It agrees with the implementer's one-off +1.1 ms and with the earlier finding that audio-off lifted frames over 34 ms. It is the price of the fix being audible. The doc says 'the audio thread's work is not on the main thread' and 'no difference beyond the spread', which this data does not support. The cost is small and acceptable for a game that is otherwise silent. Re-check on the 2-core box and soften the doc sentence.

a1.title: Planner speed buttons 2x/4x/8x no longer speed anything up on a grown web city (sliced sim at a fixed 4 ms per frame)
a1.detail: Direct A/B on the day-10 grown save, same probe, Planner, 8x button clicked and shown highlighted. Baseline daa66fd (whole ticks): clock read Day 10 17:00 -> Day 14 19:00 across the 6 HUD shots (3.4 s apart), about 4 game days in under 20 s. Fix: Day 10 17:45 -> Day 11 18:00 over about 21 s, about 1 game day, the same pace as at 1x (about 0.6x). A whole day-10 tick is 200-500 ms natively. It is about 4 ms of work per frame at 20 fps in the browser, so a tick takes roughly 100-150 frames (native: 67-196 frames per tick, mean about 100). Throughput is capped near one tick every 5-6 s whatever speed is requested. The same cap hits the pause-menu 'fast forward' feel and the live-mayor showcase, and gets worse as the city grows. The HUD still says 'Real-time pace' (that label is a separate setting, not effective speed), so the player gets no sign of the cap. Trade-off: the smoothness gain is real (fps 10.4 -> 19.7 at 8x, p99 517 -> 100 ms), but the implementer's report and docs describe only the stall win. Possible fixes: scale slice_budget_ms with speed (for example 4 ms at 1x, 16-24 ms at 8x), use a larger budget when the frame has headroom, or document that Planner fast-forward is capped on web. Measured 1x pace is unaffected. Only one run each at 8x, on a shared box.

a1.title: Medium and High web tiers cost measurably more on a grown street and buy no Planner speed; a previously saved Medium/High preset silently gets them
a1.detail: Grown day-10 street, one run each: Low busy p50 16.1 ms / 52.8 fps / 2094 draws, Medium 18.5 / 44.8 / 2458, High 18.4 / 46.1 / 3251. That is about +2.3 ms and a 13-15% fps drop, more than the +1 ms in the docs and round-1 numbers, though one run each is noisy on a shared box. Medium and High looked no cheaper or dearer than each other within that noise. Both tiers clear the stripes (0.92 and 0.50 rms) and High's frame looked clean. _load_settings in scripts/fp/fp_mode.gd still honours a saved 'quality' key, so a player who once clicked Medium or High (a no-op on web before) now gets scale 0.7/0.8, a 2048 atlas and 5-6 street lights with no notice. This was round-1 finding 8 and is not addressed. The Planner is unchanged by tiers (round 1: 44.6 / 41.4 / 42.2 ms).

a1.title: Stripe probe is a weak, timing-sensitive guard (documented, but it is the only regression check for the bias)
a1.detail: The round-1 finding is addressed: a real clear-sky pose, a row-profile metric, a limit and exit 7 now exist, and the doc is honest. Measured margins from the scratch runs: fix 0.71-1.43, old bias 2.75-2.99 at the fixed early pose but 2.39 and 1.49 for the same old bias when the pose is taken 8 s or 30 s later (p-mut8, p-mut30), i.e. the old bias would pass at those timings. The limit 2.0 sits in a gap that holds only for the early pose; any boot-time jitter that moves the pose later can hide a revert. No test or CI step runs the probe (it needs an export and a browser), and it is skipped under GF_FPS_SAVE. fp_street_bias_test remains the real regression guard, and it does catch a revert.

a2.title: At 4x and 8x sim speed the pull itself still runs in a fraction of a second (round-1 finding, not closed)
a2.detail: The haul runs on the traffic sim's dt, but the hero's reach and struggle run on real time, so only the first 0.9 s reads at speed. Measured in the final code with traffic stepped at dt*speed: person_hit to hauled is 0.68 s at 1x, 0.17 s at 4x and 0.08 s at 8x. The hero's pull beat ends the moment hauled() is true, so at 8x the 'pull' is a blink between a 0.9 s reach/struggle and a 0.3 s release. The grip no longer jumps (the hand-step clamp holds), so it is not a visual glitch, only the readability the brief asked for. Time scales available in first person are 1, 2, 4 and 8 (WS.TIME_SCALES), so 4x and 8x are reachable. Suggested fix: step the drag by real dt (divide the sim dt by ctx.sim.speed in jack_pull.haul), or hold the pull beat for HAUL_S of real time.
a2.repro: Run review-paths/r2/probe.gd with SCEN='speed:4,speed:8' (kind 'speed' steps traffic at DT*speed); read hit_t and hauled_t in the output (out_C.log: 0.17 s and 0.08 s).

a2.title: A hero knocked down (non-KO hit) mid-pull glides to the seat for 7.5 s in the 'turn' phase
a2.detail: health.hurt(5, ..., knock=true) during jack:pull does not call drive.exit (only a KO does), so the pull completes while the knock-down slides the hero away. The entry then reaches 'turn' with the hero far from the sill and _line_up sets _len = max(ALIGN_MIN, dist / ALIGN_SPEED) with no upper bound: len=7.49 s, during which _ride lerps the hero (knocked down, getting up, then in locomotion) from where he fell to the seat. He is seated at about t=13.5 s, 8 s after the pull. The end state is consistent (seated, door shut, driver on the road and up), but 'hero stuck in the door walk' lasts 7.5 s. The _line_up code is not part of the diff, but this brief asked for the hit-mid-pull state to end sanely and the new pull makes it reachable (an angry victim or a passing car can knock him down in the 0.9 s hold). Suggested fix: clamp _len in _line_up to about 1 s, or fall back to exit()/teleport to the sill when the hero is more than a metre from it.
a2.repro: review-paths/r2/probe.gd, SCEN='hurtknock:jack:pull' (out_D.log): ENTRY lines show phase=turn with len=7.49 from t=5.93 to t=13.43, then climb.

a2.title: Leftover per-car marks after a pull or an aborted hijack: traffic._taking, carjack._done and occupants._vacated
a2.detail: (a) traffic._taking keeps the id of the replaced (dead) car after every successful pull, because hold_car(id, false) is only called when _jack_id >= 0, and it is not reset in on_world_rebuilt (carjack.forget and occupants.clear are). vehicles._next_id is never reset, so ids do not repeat and the stale value is harmless today; any later reset of the counter would exempt a new car from blockers_near. (b) A hijack aborted after jack_eject (Esc, KO, police, car lost) leaves _done[id] and _vacated[id] for that car for the rest of the session (visible in probe states done=[152] vac=[152]). Behaviour is correct: the empty car is claimable without a pull and the driver is the walker on the road. It is only unbounded growth of two small dictionaries until the next rebuild.
a2.repro: probe SCEN='exit:hj:haul' then read the 'done=' and 'vac=' fields of STATE final; SCEN='none:jack:pull' shows taking=<old car id> at the end.

a2.title: Moving-car hijack: the driver pops out of the seat in one frame and the hero's hands never hold them; the pull the owner asked for is absent here
a2.detail: SEEN, coupe at 6 m/s, cam e (z_mv_e2.png, z_mv_coupe_navy_a.png): at -0.03 s the driver sits at the wheel; at +0.02 s they are already outside the car, still in the seated pose, 0.5 to 0.8 m from the sill. In the van (z_mv_van_e.png) the driver appears beside the cab at +0.02 s. From +0.07 to +0.4 s the hero stands with his back to the camera and his arms hanging at his hips, while the seated driver slides down beside the car. MEASURED (hj4 telemetry, rig that calls the real _hijack_step): hips x goes 0.39 to 0.985 in one frame on the coupe and 0.42 to 1.47 on the van. Hero wrist to nearest driver bone: coupe 0.17 to 0.2 m for the whole 0.9 s hold, then 0.12 to 0.27 m in the haul, off the body by 0.6 s; van 0.36 to 0.42 m for the whole hold (a cab too high, so the hands sit below the head clamp) and 0.39 to 1.0 m during the haul, i.e. the van driver is never held. The driver's seated pose is slid out with the seat height: hips y 0.35 to 0.38 m beside the car for about 0.3 s on the coupe, and 0.67 m on the van. The brief asked for hands on the collar and arm before the pull. The implementer disclosed a 'rigid hang' but described it as hands with a fist at the shoulder; in pixels there is no visible grip after the blow. Caveat: the rig starts the hijack directly in the jack phase (skips the leap), so the hero's pre-leap placement is the rig's, but the hold, the grips and the haul are the production code.
